rules.statement: Claude Code loads skills from the enterprise managed settings directory, ~/.claude/skills, the project .claude/skills (from the start directory up to the repository root, plus nested directories), directories passed with --add-dir, enabled plugins, and the claude.ai account. A Markdown file in .claude/commands/ is the older format and still works.
rules.quote: Save it under your home directory to get it in every project, commit it to a repository to share it with everyone who works there, or distribute it through a plugin or managed settings to reach a whole team.

rules.statement: For a skill name defined in more than one of enterprise, personal and project, enterprise wins over personal and personal wins over project. A skill wins over a same-name file in .claude/commands/.
rules.quote: Enterprise over personal, and personal over project.

rules.statement: A plugin skill is namespaced as /plugin-name:skill-name, so it loads alongside a same-name skill at any other location instead of replacing or being replaced by it.
rules.quote: Both load, because plugin skills are namespaced as

rules.statement: The combined description and when_to_use text of a skill is truncated at 1,536 characters in the skill listing. The skillListingMaxDescChars setting changes the cap.
rules.quote: the combined `description` and `when_to_use` text is truncated at 1,536 characters in the skill listing to reduce context usage

rules.statement: The skill listing is capped at a share of the model's context window, 1% by default. The skillListingBudgetFraction setting changes the share.
rules.quote: Default: 0.01, which reserves 1% of the context window

rules.statement: When the context window is not known the listing budget falls back to 8,000 characters. SLASH_COMMAND_TOOL_CHAR_BUDGET replaces the computed budget with a fixed character count.
rules.quote: The budget scales dynamically at 1% of the context window, with a fallback of 8,000 characters.

rules.statement: When the listing overflows its budget, Claude Code keeps every skill name and drops descriptions starting with the least-invoked skills, so the most-used skills keep their full text.
rules.quote: When the listing overflows, Claude Code drops descriptions starting with the skills you invoke least, so the skills you use most keep their full text.

rules.statement: The skillOverrides setting does not apply to plugin skills. Plugin skills are managed through /plugin.
rules.quote: Overrides don’t apply to plugin skills, which you manage through /plugin.

rules.topic: skillOverrides key of a synced claude.ai skill
rules.statement: A skill synced from claude.ai is listed as anthropic-skills:<name>, and a skillOverrides entry under that full name always applies to it; when both keys are set the full name wins. An entry under the bare name applies to it only while no other loaded command holds that name. A user or project skill holds its folder name and its frontmatter name, and takes the entry for itself only under its folder name. A user or project command holds the name it is listed under (its file name, or ns:name in a subfolder, which no bare name equals) and not its frontmatter name. A plugin skill or command holds a name only when its frontmatter gives that name without a colon; its folder or file name alone does not hold, and overrides never apply to it. Names are compared without regard to case.
rules.quote: answer only to anthropic-skills:<name>
rules.evidence: Read from the Claude Code 2.1.292 binary: the override lookup tries the command's own name and then its unqualified name, and a synced skill whose bare name is reserved has no unqualified name; the bare name is reserved when the skill lost its bare alias because the name, display name or an alias of another loaded command equals it, and a plugin skill or command gets an alias only from a frontmatter name without a colon. The same reading puts the commands and bundled skills of Claude Code itself in that set; this was not probed. Probes on 2.1.292 (2026-10-07), each reading the skill_listing attachment of a new session. First: "google-workspace": "off" left anthropic-skills:google-workspace listed beside the plugin skill jstack:google-workspace, whose frontmatter names it, and the entry left once the key was "anthropic-skills:google-workspace"; twelve bare keys with no namesake hid their synced skills. In further sessions, with bare keys turned off in project settings: with no namesake the synced skills left; a project skill xlsx and a top-level project command pdf held the name and were hidden themselves; a plugin command probe:docx without a frontmatter name did not hold docx; a project command in a subfolder, listed as ns:pptx, did not hold pptx. Also: a plugin command whose frontmatter says name: docx held docx, as did plugin commands declared in the manifest; a plugin skill in a folder xlsx without a frontmatter name did not hold xlsx; a project skill in folder pptx named zz-renamed-deck held pptx and was hidden by the key; a project skill in folder zz-folder-sheet named pdf held pdf and stayed listed; a project skill PPTX held pptx while the key pptx did not apply to it; a top-level project command with frontmatter name xlsx did not hold xlsx; a plugin skill whose frontmatter name contains a colon and a project agent did not hold the bare name; and with both keys set the full-name key decided. Re-check: grep -a -c -F 'answer only to anthropic-skills:<name>' ~/.local/share/claude/versions/<version> (on 2.1.292 the lookup itself reads 'bareNameReserved?void 0:'), then set a bare and a full-name key and read the skill_listing attachment of a new session transcript under ~/.claude/projects.

rules.statement: A skill or command is listed to the model unless disable-model-invocation is set or skillOverrides turns it off or to user-invocable-only. A plugin skill or command is listed only when its frontmatter gives a description or a when_to_use; one with neither costs nothing in the listing, can still be typed, and is not blocked from model invocation the way disable-model-invocation blocks it.
rules.quote: e.loadedFrom==="commands_DEPRECATED"||e.hasUserSpecifiedDescription||!!e.whenToUse
rules.evidence: Read from the Claude Code 2.1.291 binary: the predicate that selects model-listed commands requires type "prompt", no disableModelInvocation, no off or user-invocable-only override, and one of: a built-in, bundled, skills-directory, synced, attached-folder or .claude/commands entry, a user-specified description, or a when_to_use. Plugin entries are none of the former, so they need the description. The Skill tool refuses only disable-model-invocation entries ('cannot be used with ... tool due to disable-model-invocation'). Measured on 2.1.292 (2026-10-07) with a probe plugin holding one command with a description and one without: the model's skill list showed only the described command, and the Skill tool ran the undescribed one when asked for it by name. Re-check: grep -a -c -F 'e.loadedFrom==="commands_DEPRECATED"||e.hasUserSpecifiedDescription||!!e.whenToUse' ~/.local/share/claude/versions/<version>

rules.statement: Claude Code puts its own skills and prompt commands in the same listing and under the same budget as user and plugin skills. They are not files in the profile, so the audit counts them as an observed figure, about 6,600 characters on 2.1.292 (between 5,700 and 6,600 across sessions), and treats them as kept first: when the listing is over budget, bundled entries keep their full text and the other entries share what is left.
rules.quote: source==="bundled"
rules.evidence: Measured on Claude Code 2.1.292 (2026-10-07) from the skill_listing attachment of probe sessions: 14 entries without a plugin prefix that are not the user's own (dataviz, code-review, update-config, schedule, run, loop, workflow-authoring, plugin-authoring, keybindings-help, fewer-permission-prompts, simplify, claude-api, security-review, init) totalled 5,690 characters in one session and 6,622 in another. Read from the Claude Code 2.1.291 binary: the function that logs 'Skill listing over budget' keeps entries whose source is bundled at full length before it distributes the remaining budget. Which host entries count as bundled, and so are kept first, was not established for each one; treating the whole block as kept first is the conservative reading. Re-check: grep -a -c -F 'source==="bundled"' ~/.local/share/claude/versions/<version>, and in a session transcript under ~/.claude/projects read the attachment of type skill_listing and sum the lines whose name has no plugin prefix and is not one of your own skills.

rules.statement: The listing budget in characters is the context window in tokens x characters per token x the budget fraction, rounded down. Characters per token depend on the model: 4 for the claude-3 family, opus 4-0, 4-1, 4-5 and 4-6, sonnet 4-0, 4-5 and 4-6 and haiku 4-5, and 3 for every other model, so current models get 3. With no known window the computation uses 200000 tokens, which gives the documented 8,000 characters only at 4 characters per token.
rules.quote: return JI.has(r)?4:3}
rules.evidence: Read from the Claude Code 2.1.291 binary. The listing sent to the model is built by the function that logs 'Skill listing over budget'; /context uses a sibling with the same arithmetic. Its caller passes the main-loop model's context window and the characters per token from a small function that returns 4 when no model is given and otherwise normalizes the model id (dots and underscores become hyphens) and returns JI.has(id)?4:3, where JI is a Set of the 4-character models declared just before it. The budget function is cXe(window, cpt=4): the SLASH_COMMAND_TOOL_CHAR_BUDGET value when it parses to a nonzero number, else Math.max(1, Math.floor((window ?? 200000) x cpt x fraction)), with the fraction setting or the default 0.01 and the constants declared side by side as =0.01,k=4,m=200000. docs/skill-routing-principles-20260915.md (section 5, observed in 2.1.272) recorded 4 for every model; 2.1.291 differs. Re-check: grep -a -o -E '.{60}\.replace\(/\[\._\]/g,"-"\);return [A-Za-z0-9_$]+\.has\([a-z]\)\?4:3\}' on ~/.local/share/claude/versions/<version> prints the function and the end of the set before it; grep -a -o -E 'function [A-Za-z0-9_$]+\(e,n=[A-Za-z0-9_$]+\)\{let r=[A-Za-z0-9_$]+\(process\.env\.SLASH_COMMAND_TOOL_CHAR_BUDGET\);if\(r\)return r;.{110}' prints the budget function. When the set or the 4 and 3 change, update CPT4_MODEL in scripts/analyze.ts.

rules.statement: A listed skill or command is the line `- name: text` and costs the name plus 4 characters plus the text; an entry shown without a description is `- name` and costs the name plus 2. The text is the description, followed by ` - ` and when_to_use when there is one, cut to the per-skill cap. The lines are joined with newlines, one character for each entry but the first, and the host counts each line in display width, so a CJK character counts 2. The listing is over budget when this sum exceeds the budget.
rules.quote: e.whenToUse?`${e.description} - ${e.whenToUse}`:e.description
rules.evidence: Read from the Claude Code 2.1.291 binary, in the function that logs 'Skill listing over budget'. Each entry becomes `- ${name}` or, with a description, `- ${name}: ${text}` where text is the description joined to when_to_use with ' - ' and cut to the cap (cut text ends in an ellipsis, so it keeps the cap's length); the total is the sum of the line widths, measured with Bun.stringWidth (ambiguous characters narrow), plus entries - 1 for the newlines. The sibling used by /context adds name + 4 + text for a full entry and name + 2 for a name-only one. The name is the command's name, or `name (display name)` for a skill whose display name differs. Re-check: grep -a -A3 -F 'Skill listing over budget: ${' on ~/.local/share/claude/versions/<version> prints the whole function, and grep -a -o -F 'e.whenToUse?`${e.description} - ${e.whenToUse}`:e.description' finds the text join. A changed join, prefix or separator means the per-entry cost in scripts/analyze.ts (claudeRows) must follow.

rules.statement: When the listing exceeds its budget every entry first costs its name-only line, and the rest of the budget goes to descriptions in order of usageCount x max(0.5^(daysSinceUse/7), 0.1), highest first, ties in listing order. An entry whose description does not fit stays name-only and the next entries are still tried, so a smaller description can fit after a larger one was skipped. A skill with no recorded use scores 0. Usage is looked up under the command's own name: the qualified name for a plugin skill (jstack:plan), the short name for a skill synced from claude.ai (pdf).
rules.quote: .usageCount*Math.max(
rules.evidence: Read from the Claude Code 2.1.291 binary, in the function that logs 'Skill listing over budget'. Entries set to name-only in skillOverrides stay name-only and bundled skills always keep their description; both are charged first. The other entries are sorted by the score function, highest first (a stable sort, so ties keep the listing order), and visited once with if(extra<=left){keep; left-=extra}, where extra is the full line minus the name-only line and left starts at the budget minus the name-only total. The score is usageCount*Math.max(Math.pow(0.5, days/7), 0.1) for skillUsage[name] in ~/.claude.json, and 0 without a record; usage is written under the dispatched command's name. docs/skill-routing-principles-20260915.md (section 5, observed in 2.1.272) first recorded the score; its lowest-first drop order is superseded by this keep order. Re-check: grep -a -A3 -F 'Skill listing over budget: ${' on ~/.local/share/claude/versions/<version> prints the loop after the warning text, and grep -a -o -E '.{80}\.usageCount\*Math\.max\(.{40}' prints the score. The behavior was read from code, not measured at two context windows.

rules.statement: For subagents sharing a name Claude Code uses the highest-priority location: managed settings, then the --agents flag, then .claude/agents/, then ~/.claude/agents/, then a plugin's agents/ directory.
rules.quote: When multiple subagents share the same name, Claude Code uses the one from the higher-priority location.

rules.statement: When the combined descriptions of the subagents, built-in ones excluded, pass 15,000 tokens, Claude Code shows a warning at startup and still loads every subagent.
rules.quote: When the combined descriptions of your subagents, except the built-in ones, exceed 15,000 tokens

rules.statement: A server defined in more than one place connects once, using the whole entry from the highest-precedence source: local, then project, then user, then plugin-provided servers, then claude.ai connectors. Duplicates across the local, project and user scopes are matched by name; plugin servers and connectors are matched by endpoint, so one that points at the same URL or command as an enabled server above is a duplicate. Fields are not merged across scopes.
rules.quote: It matches plugins and connectors by endpoint, so one that points at the same URL or command as an enabled server above counts as a duplicate.

rules.statement: Tool search is on by default, so only MCP tool names and server instructions load at session start and tool definitions are deferred until Claude needs them.
rules.quote: Only tool names and server instructions load at session start

rules.statement: Claude Code truncates each MCP tool description and each server's instructions at 2,048 characters by default. CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_MCP_DESCRIPTION_LENGTH changes the limit.
rules.quote: Claude Code truncates each tool description and each server’s instructions at 2,048 characters by default.

rules.topic: plugin hooks next to settings hooks
rules.statement: When a plugin is enabled its hooks merge with the user and project hooks. The same handler in several settings files runs once, but a plugin's copy of the same handler stays separate and runs in addition.
rules.quote: A plugin’s or skill’s copy of the same handler stays separate.

rules.statement: claude plugin details reports a loaded plugin's component inventory and its projected token cost, the always-on tokens the plugin adds to every session.
rules.quote: Show a plugin’s component inventory and its projected token cost.

rules.statement: Codex scans .agents/skills in every directory from the working directory up to the repository root, then $HOME/.agents/skills, /etc/codex/skills, and the skills bundled with Codex.
rules.quote: For repositories, Codex scans `.agents/skills` in every directory from your current working directory up to the repository root.

rules.statement: Codex does not merge skills that share a name. Both can appear in skill selectors.
rules.quote: If two skills share the same `name`, Codex doesn’t merge them; both can appear in skill selectors.

rules.statement: The initial skills list, which includes each skill's file path, uses at most 2% of the model's context window.
rules.quote: this list uses at most 2% of the model’s context window

rules.statement: When the context window is unknown the initial skills list is limited to 8,000 characters.
rules.quote: or 8,000 characters when the context window is unknown

rules.statement: skills.max_context_tokens sets the token budget for the available-skills catalog, which defaults to 2% of the context window. Explicit values are capped at 10000 tokens.
rules.quote: Explicit values are capped at `10000` tokens.

rules.statement: When many skills are installed Codex shortens skill descriptions first. For large skill sets it may then omit some skills from the initial list and show a warning.
rules.quote: If many skills are installed, Codex shortens skill descriptions first. For large skill sets, Codex may omit some skills from the initial list and show a warning.

rules.topic: how Codex prints a skill's path
rules.statement: Codex lists each skill with its path as a root alias plus the path under that root, for example `(file: r11/workflow/plan/SKILL.md)`. The aliases are defined once in a `### Skill roots` section of the same listing, and the model expands the matching alias before it opens a skill file. The audit counts each path as a 4-character alias plus the path under its skills root.
rules.quote: expand the matching root alias first from `### Skill roots`
rules.evidence: Read from the Codex 0.160.1 binary and from Codex session logs. The binary holds the skill-usage instruction text "If its location is a short aliased path, expand the matching root alias first from `### Skill roots`, then open and read its `SKILL.md` completely before taking task actions." and says a location may be "an absolute filesystem path, a short aliased path, or a non-filesystem reference". Session logs under ~/.codex/sessions (rollout-*.jsonl) hold the rendered listing: a `### Skill roots` block of lines such as `r0` = `<home>/.agents/skills`, then skill lines ending in `(file: r11/workflow/plan/SKILL.md)`. The audit's 4 characters for the alias is the width of `r11/`; an alias counts 3 characters from r0 to r9 and 5 from r100, and the `### Skill roots` block itself is not counted. Re-check: on the native binary of the installed Codex (for the npm package, node_modules/@openai/codex-<platform>/vendor/<triple>/bin/codex under the package directory; resolve symlinks from the codex command) run grep -a -o -F 'expand the matching root alias first from `### Skill roots`' and grep -a -o -E 'short aliased path.{80}'; in a recent session log run grep -a -o -E '.{40}\(file: r[0-9]+/[^)]*\)' on a rollout file. A changed literal means the path cost in scripts/analyze.ts (codexPathChars) must follow.

rules.statement: Custom agents are standalone TOML files under ~/.codex/agents/ for personal agents and .codex/agents/ for project-scoped agents.
rules.quote: To define your own custom agents, add standalone TOML files under `~/.codex/agents/` for personal agents or `.codex/agents/` for project-scoped agents.

rules.statement: A custom agent whose name matches a built-in agent such as explorer takes precedence over the built-in one.
rules.quote: If a custom agent name matches a built-in agent such as `explorer`, your custom agent takes precedence.

rules.statement: MCP servers are configured in mcp_servers tables of ~/.codex/config.toml, or of a project .codex/config.toml in trusted projects only.
rules.quote: By default this is `~/.codex/config.toml`, but you can also scope MCP servers to a project with `.codex/config.toml` (trusted projects only).

rules.statement: Codex loads the matching hooks of every source (user and repository hooks.json and config.toml, managed layers, enabled plugins). A higher-precedence layer does not replace lower-precedence hooks.
rules.quote: If more than one hook source exists, Codex loads all matching hooks.

rules.statement: codex debug prompt-input renders the exact model-visible prompt input list as JSON. The command is marked experimental.
rules.quote: Render the exact model-visible prompt input list as JSON.

rules.statement: A skill name is 1 to 64 characters of lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens. It must not start or end with a hyphen or contain consecutive hyphens, and it must match the parent directory name.
rules.quote: Must be 1-64 characters

rules.statement: A skill description is 1 to 1024 characters and describes both what the skill does and when to use it.
rules.quote: Must be 1-1024 characters
